Problem: A solid wooden rectangular prism measures $3 \times 5 \times 12$. The prism is cut in half by a vertical cut through four vertices, creating two congruent triangular-based prisms. What is the surface area of one of these triangular-based prisms?

<reflection>
The original rectangular prism has dimensions 3, 5, and 12. The vertical cut through four vertices creates two congruent triangular-based prisms. The goal is to find the surface area of one of these triangular prisms.
This orientation makes the 12-length the vertical height, so the vertical cut passes through a diagonal of the 3×5 face. The intended vertical cut uses the 5×12 face as the base and the 3-length as the height, giving triangular bases with legs 5 and 12.
Orient the prism with base 5×12 and height 3, then cut vertically along a diagonal of that base.
</reflection>
